ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p187/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p187/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p187/r2.claim: Rain and opened earth pores are signs of God’s power and mercy; no one else can provide these conditions on which the earth’s benefits depend.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p187/r2.anchor: Neither is anyone else in the position to send down rain from the skies nor to open the pores of the earth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p187/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p187/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p187/r3.claim: The food argument parallels the creation argument: both establish resurrection’s possibility, cite providential signs, and culminate in accountability and reward or punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p187/r3.anchor: the sequence of premises in the argument presented is the same

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:26-36/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:26-36/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:26-36/r1.claim: God splits the earth for plants or plowing, attributing the act to Himself as its cause.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:26-36/r1.anchor: { ثم شققنا الأرض شقا } أي بالنبات أو بالكراب، وأسند الشق إلى نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

JISHUMI:v10p7291/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r2.claim: God splits the earth so the fragile plant can root and send up its shoot.
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r2.anchor: ثم شققنا الأرض شقا ليخرج النبات مع ضعفه، فيرسخ عرقه ويظهر فرعه

JISHUMI:v10p7291/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r3.claim: One explanation is that God directly separates the earth's parts and brings the crop out without an intermediary cause.
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r3.anchor: أحدهما: أنه تعالى يشققها بأن يفرق بين أجزائها، ويخرج الزرع منها

JISHUMI:v10p7291/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r4.claim: The other explanation is that forces in the plant push earth-parts outward, so the earth is split through the plant as a cause.
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r4.anchor: وثانيها: أنه يجعل في أجزاء النبات اعتمادات تخرج أجزاء الأرض

JISHUMI:v10p7291/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r5.claim: The first account makes the split God's act without a cause; the second makes it an act through a cause.
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r5.anchor: فعلى الوجه الأول هو فعله بغير سبب، وعلى الثاني فعله بسبب

TABATABAI:80:25-36/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:25-36/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:25-36/r1.claim: The open reading “anā” begins a detailed but necessarily incomplete account of God's provisioning of human food; ordinary explanation cannot encompass the full system and its cosmic relations.
TABATABAI:80:25-36/r1.anchor: وهو بيان تفصيلي لتدبيره تعالى طعام الإنسان نعم هو مرحلة ابتدائية من التفصيل

TABATABAI:80:25-36/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:25-36/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:25-36/r3.claim: The earth splitting is plants breaking through soil; “then” and the following “so” reflect the sequence from rain to growth and grain.
TABATABAI:80:25-36/r3.anchor: ظاهره شق الأرض بالنبات الخارج منها ولذا عطف على صب الماء بثم وعطف عليه إنبات الحب بالفاء

ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r15.claim: Rain makes dry, lifeless earth stir and swell before it cracks and produces plants, a marvel attributed to God.
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r15.anchor: yağmurlar nüzûlüyle ihtizâza gelip feyizlenmeye, sonra çatlayıp nebâtât çıkarmaya başlayan

ZAJJAJ:v5p285/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p285/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p285/r5.claim: God split the earth by means of vegetation.

NASHR:v1p293/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p293/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p293/r5.claim: The author distinguishes the isolated assimilation in والأرض شقا: the first phrase needs care to avoid a repeated sound, while the latter is light because a fatḥa follows sukūn; a lone chain reports assimilation, but practice follows the majority.
NASHR:v1p293/r5.anchor: يمكن أن يقال في الفرق: إن الإدغام لما كان القارئ يحتاج إلى التحفظ في التلفظ بها من ظهور تكرارها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p46/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God split the earth with plants in a wondrous way fitted to each plant's size, shape, form, and appearance.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46/r1.anchor: أي بالنبات كما قال ابن عباس شقا بديعا لائقا بما يشقها من النبات

ALUSI-FULL:v30p46/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46/r2.claim: Another view takes the splitting to mean plowing; attributing it to God is figurative attribution to the cause, though God is the true creator, but the author notes that thumma counts against this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46/r2.anchor: وقيل شقها بالكراب وإسناده إلى ضميره تعالى مجاز من باب الإسناد إلى السبب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p46/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46/r3.claim: An action is properly attributed to the agent in whom it subsists, not to the one who produces it in another; this is why the agent's active participle is derived from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46/r3.anchor: أن إسناد الفعل حقيقة لمن قام به لا من صدر عنه إيجادا ولهذا يشتق اسم الفاعل له

ALUSI-FULL:v30p46#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46#2/r3.claim: A defense of the plowing interpretation says the conjunction need not make every limitation of the first action apply to the second; plowing may be illustrative or may mean digging, since it does not suit grapes, olives, and palms.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46#2/r3.anchor: وأجيب بأنه ليس من لوازم العطف تقييد المعطوف بجميع ما قيد به المعطوف عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p46#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes the splitting occur through springs, taking the water poured out as rain and the rivers as its flow; al-Alusi objects that thumma puts the split after the water.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46#2/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المراد شقها بالعيون على أن المراد بصب الماء أمطار المطر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p46#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46#2/r6.claim: A defense says spring water itself comes from rain rather than vapors stored underground; al-Alusi calls the proposal far-fetched and contrived.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p46#2/r6.anchor: ودفعا بأن ماء العيون من المطر لا من الأبخرة المحتسبة في الأرض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p338#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p338#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p338#2/r9.claim: God split the earth by bringing forth plants.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p329/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p329/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p329/r9.claim: After rain, God varies regions and vegetation, then splits the earth with fragile plants that break through even very hard ground.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p329/r9.anchor: بعد مهلة من إنزال الماء , وفاوتنا بينها في البلاد والنبات

DURR-FULL:v8p420/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p420/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p420/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the earth is split open for the growth of vegetation.
DURR-FULL:v8p420/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس {إنا صببنا الماء صبا} قال: المطر {ثم شققنا الأرض شقا} عن النبات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p131/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p131/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p131/r1.claim: Attributing pouring, splitting, and growing to God is a rational metaphor; for pouring and planting, usage has made the attribution almost literal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p131/r1.anchor: الإسناد مجاز عقلي في الأفعال الثلاثة . وقد شاع في { صببنا } و { أنبتنا } حتى ساوى الحقيقة العقلية .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p131/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p131/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p131/r2.claim: The accusatives ṣabban and shaqqan are cognate accusatives emphasizing their verbs; their indefinite form permits a magnifying, wonder-inducing sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p131/r2.anchor: وانتصب { صبا } و { شقا } على المفعول المطلق ل { صببنا } و { شققنا } مؤكدا لعامله ليتأتى تنوينه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r1.claim: Shaqq is separating what had been joined; here it is the soil's surface split by water, a plow or hoe, or summer sun so autumn and winter rain can penetrate it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r1.anchor: والشق : الإبعاد بين ما كان متصلا . والمراد هنا شق سطح الأرض بخرق الماء فيه أو بآلة كالمحراث والمسحاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r2.claim: The actions are attributed to God because He orders the effective causes, establishes their laws, and inspires people to use them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r2.anchor: وإسناد الصب والشق والإنبات إلى ضمير الجلالة لأن الله مقدر نظام الأسباب المؤثرة في ذلك ، ومحكم نواميسها وملهم الناس استعمالها .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r3.claim: Attributing pouring, splitting, and growing to God is a rational metaphor; for pouring and planting, usage has made the attribution almost literal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r3.anchor: فالإسناد مجاز عقلي في الأفعال الثلاثة . وقد شاع في { صببنا } و { أنبتنا } حتى ساوى الحقيقة العقلية .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r4.claim: The accusatives ṣabban and shaqqan are cognate accusatives emphasizing their verbs; indefinite marking conveys magnification and wonder suited to each thing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#28/r4.anchor: وانتصب { صبا } و { شقا } على المفعول المطلق ل { صببنا } و { شققنا } مؤكدا لعامله ليتأتى تنوينه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33#3/r1.claim: God split the earth open with vegetation growing through it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p323/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p323/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p323/r7.claim: Water enters the earth’s depths and permeates embedded seeds, making them sprout, rise, and emerge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p323/r7.anchor: (ثم شققنا الأرض شقا) أي: أسكناه فيها فدخل في تخومها وتخلل في أجزاء الحب المودع فيها فنبت وارتفع وظهر على وجه الأرض،

JISHUMI:v10p7288/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7288/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7288/r10.claim: Shaqq, ṣadʿ, faṭr, and farj are synonyms for splitting/opening.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r4.claim: The earth’s splitting can mean the opening made by plants, or furrows cut by ox-drawn plows; the action is ascribed to God as its ultimate cause.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r4.anchor: وشققنا : من شق الأرض بالنبات ويجوز أن يكون من شقها بالكراب على البقر ؛ وأسند الشك إلى نفسه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r4.claim: The earth’s splitting can mean the opening made by plants, or furrows cut by ox-drawn plows; the action is ascribed to God as its ultimate cause.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r4.anchor: وشققنا : من شق الأرض بالنبات ويجوز أن يكون من شقها بالكراب على البقر ؛ وأسند الشك إلى نفسه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r10.claim: The splitting of the earth is by the growth of plants.

MUQATIL:80:24-32/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:24-32/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:24-32/r4.claim: God split the earth to bring forth plants and trees.
MUQATIL:80:24-32/r4.anchor: يعني عن النبت والشجر { فأنبتنا فيها حبا

MUQATIL:80:24-32/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:24-32/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:80:24-32/r12.claim: The Prophet said that people were created from seven, provided for from seven, and brought forth upon seven.
MUQATIL:80:24-32/r12.anchor: خلقتم من سبع، ورزقتم من سبع، وخرجتم على سبع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p318#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p318#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p318#6/r1.claim: God split the earth open with vegetation growing through it.

BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r11.claim: After the rain, God split the soil for the plants; thumma marks that the splitting follows the pouring.
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r11.anchor: ولما كان الشق بعد الصب أورد كلمة ثم الشق بالفارسية شكافتن

BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r12.claim: Shaqqan is a wondrous splitting suited to the plants’ differing sizes, shapes, and forms.
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r12.anchor: بديعا لائقا بما يشقها من النبات صغرا وكبرا وشكلا وهيئة

QURTUBI-FULL:80:25-31/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:25-31/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:25-31/r2.claim: God split the earth by plants growing through it.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:25-31/r2.anchor: { ثم شققنا الأرض شقا }: أي بالنبات

STUDYQURAN:80:26/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:26/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:26/r1.claim: Vegetation emerges through fissures that split the earth; related descriptions of vegetation and the earth revived by water occur at 6:99, 29:63, 30:24, 31:10, 35:27, and 39:21.
STUDYQURAN:80:26/r1.anchor: Vegetation comes through the fissures, splitting the earth.

TUSTARI:80:26/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:80:26/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:80:26/r1.claim: In the inward reading, the earth is the heart: God splits it and grows there the blossoms of spirit, intellect, faith, and gnosis.
TUSTARI:80:26/r1.anchor: وهو القلب { شقا } [26]، فأنبت فيها من ألوان الزهرة

TUSTARI:80:26/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:80:26/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:80:26/r2.claim: The Prophet compares the Qur'an to a blossom in hearts, faith to rain planting richness, and greed to dew planting hypocrisy like grass.
TUSTARI:80:26/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ألا إن القرآن زهرة في القلوب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p228/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p228/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p228/r1.claim: God split the earth open through vegetation.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:20-28/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:20-28/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:20-28/r8.claim: The earth is split open by the growing plants.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r1.claim: After summarizing divine favors concerning human existence and nature in verses 18–20, the passage recalls external blessings that sustain human life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r1.anchor: Yukarıda 18-20. âyetlerde insanın var oluşu ve mahiyetine ilişkin ilâhî lütuflar özetlenmişti; burada ise onu çevreleyen ve varlığını sürdürmesi için gerekli ve faydalı olan haricî nimetlerin başlıcaları hatırlatılmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r2.claim: The reminders aim to inform people of God's great power and strengthen faith, and to move them to grateful worship and obedience in response to His favors.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r2.anchor: Bu hatırlatmanın amacı da hem muhatabı Allah’ın kudretinin büyüklüğü hakkında bilgilendirip iman etmesini veya inancını güçlendirmesini sağlamak hem de onu bu lütuflarından dolayı Allah’a minnet ve şükran hisleriyle ibadet etmeye, buyruklarına göre yaşamaya yöneltmektir.

THALABI:v10p133/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p133/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p133/r7.claim: The earth is split open by vegetation.

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r31.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r31.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r31.claim: In the inward reading, God pours the water of mercy onto hardened hearts, softening them for repentance.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r31.anchor: صببنا ماء الرحمة على القلوب القاسية فلانت للتوبة
